paper.title: A Bandit Approach to Multiple Testing with False Discovery Control

settings.name_in_paper: Identifying arms with means above a known threshold mu_0 with FDR/FWER control and TPR/FWPD detection (fixed confidence)
unmapped: Known threshold mu_0; null arms have mean equal to (or at most) mu_0, alternatives have mean > mu_0
Goal: output anytime set S_t with FDR-delta or FWER-delta false alarm control, and minimal time tau after which TPR-delta,tau or FWPD-delta,tau holds
No stopping: algorithm runs indefinitely; sample complexity is the time after which detection guarantees hold
Learner uses an anytime confidence interval phi(t,delta) <= sqrt(c_phi log(log2(2t)/delta)/t)
settings.definition_quote: Consider $n$ distributions (or arms) and a game where at each time $t$, the player chooses an arm $i \in [n]$ and immediately observes a reward $X_{i,t} \overset{iid}{\sim} \nu_i$ where $X_{i,t} \in [0,1]$ ... For a \emph{known} threshold $\mu_0$, define the sets $\H_1 = \{ i \in [n]: \mu_i > \mu_0 \}$ and $\H_0 = \{ i \in [n] : \mu_i = \mu_0 \}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Threshold multiple testing, Gaussian instances (lower bound for uniform allocation)
unmapped: Known threshold mu_0; arms in H_1 have mean mu_0+Delta (or Delta/2 vs -Delta/2), nulls have mean mu_0, unit variance
Lower bound only for algorithms sampling each arm equally (uniform allocation)
settings.definition_quote:
For any $\H_1 \subseteq [n]$ such that $|\H_1|=k$ define an instance $(\{
u_i\}_{i=1}^n, \mu_0)$ with $\mu_0 = 0$, $
u_i =\mathcal{N}(\Delta, 1)$ for $i\in \H_1$ , $
u_i =\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ for $i\in \H_0$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1 (UCB sampling with anytime Benjamini-Hochberg selection, plus Bonferroni-like set R_t for FWER)
Uniform allocation with anytime BH selection (Algorithm 2)

symbols.Delta_thr: min_{i in H_1} mu_i - mu_0, gap of the weakest alternative above the threshold

conditions: FDR-delta control on S_t and TPR-delta,T detection

source.label: thm:FDR_TPR
source.quote: For all $t \in \mathbb{N}$ we have $\E[\frac{|\calS_t \cap \H_0|}{|\calS_t| \vee 1}] \leq \delta$. Moreover, with probability at least $1-2\delta$ there exists a $T$ such that T \lesssim \min\{n \Delta^{-2} \log( \log(\Delta^{-2})/\delta), \sum_{i \in \H_0} \Delta_i^{-2} \log( \log(\Delta_i^{-2})/\delta) + \sum_{i \in \H_1} \Delta_i^{-2} \log( n \log(\Delta_i^{-2})/\delta)\} and $\E[\frac{|\calS_t \cap \H_1|}{|\H_1|}] \geq 1-\delta$ for all $t \geq T$.

results.notes: First argument of the min. n = K arms. Sample complexity is the time after which TPR holds, guaranteed with probability >= 1-2delta.

symbols.sum_H0: sum over null arms i in H_0, with Delta_i = min_{j in H_1} mu_j - mu_i
symbols.sum_H1: sum over alternative arms i in H_1, with Delta_i = mu_i - mu_0

conditions: FDR-delta control on S_t and TPR-delta,T detection
results.notes: Second argument of the min; Delta_i defined differently for H_0 and H_1 arms (not the canonical gap to mu_star).

symbols.k_1: |H_1|, number of arms with mean above the threshold

conditions: FDR-delta control on S_t and FWPD detection (H_1 subset of S_t for t >= T)
tuning: FWPD variant: xi_t = max{2|S_t|, 5 log(1/delta)/(3(1-4delta))}, nu_t = max{|S_t|,1}

source.label: thm:FDR_FWPD
source.quote: For all $t \in \mathbb{N}$ we have $\E[\frac{|\calS_t \cap \H_0|}{|\calS_t| \vee 1}] \leq \delta$. Moreover, with probability at least $1-5\delta$, there exists a $T$ such that T \lesssim  (n-|\H_1|) \Delta^{-2} \log (  \max\{|\H_1|, \log\log(n/\delta)\} \log(\Delta^{-2})/ \delta)  + |\H_1| \Delta^{-2} \log ( \log(\Delta^{-2})/ \delta) and $\H_1 \subseteq \calS_t$ for all $t \geq T$.

conditions: FWER control on R_t (H_0 cap R_t empty for all t) and FWPD detection on R_t

source.label: thm:FWER_FWPD
source.quote: Moreover, with probability at least $1-6\delta$, we have $\H_0 \cap \calR_t = \emptyset$ for all $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and there exists a $T$ such that T \lesssim  (n-|\H_1|) \Delta^{-2} \log (  \max\{|\H_1|, \log\log(n/\delta)\} \log(\Delta^{-2}) / \delta) + |\H_1| \Delta^{-2} \log ( \max\{n-(1-2\delta(1+4\delta))|\H_1|, \log\log(n/\delta)\}\log(\Delta^{-2}) / \delta) and $\H_1 \subseteq \calR_t$ for all $t \geq T$.

results.notes: Implies H_1 = R_t for t >= T on the event.

symbols.eta_thr: eta = 1 - 3 delta - sqrt(2 delta log(1/delta)/|H_1|) as defined in the theorem

conditions: FWER control on R_t and TPR-delta detection on R_t

source.label: thm:FWER_TPR
source.quote: Moreover, with probability at least $1-7\delta$ we have $\H_0 \cap \calR_t = \emptyset$ for all $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and there exists a $T$ such that T \lesssim  (n-|\H_1|) \Delta^{-2} \log (  \log(\Delta^{-2})/ \delta) + |\H_1| \Delta^{-2} \log ( \max\{n-(1-\eta)|\H_1|, \log\log(n\log(1/\delta)/\delta)\}\log(\Delta^{-2}) / \delta) and $\E[\frac{|\calR_t \cap \H_1|}{|\H_1|}] \geq 1-\delta$ for all $t \geq T$, where $\eta=( 1 - 3\delta- \sqrt{2\delta \log(1/\delta)/|\H_1|})$.

results.notes: The main-text eta (1-3delta-...) is written so that the expression uses (1-eta); the appendix restatement instead uses (1-2delta). Recorded as in main text. Note the oddity: with eta as defined, (1-eta) is small, which seems inconsistent with proof; recorded verbatim.

symbols.sum_H1: sum over arms in H_1 with Delta_i = mu_i - mu_0

conditions: on event E_5, probability at least 1-delta

In addition, in the case of successive elimination, if $\eta = ...$, then on the event $\mathcal{E}_5$ (which holds with probability greater than $1-\delta$) then there exists a $T$ such that T \lesssim \min\{ ... \}

results.notes: Up to n pulls per round; T counts total samples. Baseline result.

conditions: on event E_5, probability at least 1-delta

source.quote: and in the case of Uniform allocation, T \lesssim n \Delta^{-2} \log(\tfrac{n}{(1-\eta)|\H_1|} \log(\Delta^{-2})/\delta)

results.notes: Event E_5 stated for successive elimination; uniform case uses same reasoning.

conditions: arms in H_1 are N(Delta,1), nulls N(0,1), mu_0 = 0
algorithm must be FDR-delta and TPR-delta,tau for all H_1 of size k simultaneously

source.label: thm:uniform_fdr_lower_bound
source.quote: Fix $\delta < 1/40$, $\Delta > 0$. and $k < n/2$. ... Any algorithm that samples each arm an equal number of times before outputting a set $\calS \subseteq [n]$ after $\tau$ total samples, and is FDR-$\delta$ and TPR-$\delta,\tau$ ... must satisfy $t \gtrsim n\Delta^{-2}\log{(n/k)}$.

results.notes: Applies only to uniform-allocation algorithms. Probability type: guarantee on criteria in expectation; marked expectation loosely.

conditions: mu_0 = -Delta/2, arms N(Delta/2,1) in H_1 and N(-Delta/2,1) in H_0
algorithm must be FWER-delta and FWPD-delta,tau for all H_1 subset of [n] simultaneously

source.label: thm:uniform_fwer_lower_bound
source.quote: Fix $\delta < 3/8$ and $\Delta >0$. ... Any algorithm that samples each arm an equal number of times before outputting a set $\calS \subseteq [n]$ after $\tau$ total samples, and is FWER-$\delta$ and FWPD-$\delta,\tau$ on $(\{\nu_i\}_{i=1}^n, \mu_0)$ for all $\H_1 \subseteq [n]$ simultaneously, must satisfy $\tau \gtrsim n\Delta^{-2} \log(n)$.
